raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

On SM12x GPUs (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, RTX 50xx, GB10) the 8-bit Marlin MoE kernel has no fitting thread tile for MXFP8 expert shapes whose intermediate size is not a multiple of 128, and fails at warm-up:

```
RuntimeError: marlin_mm, csrc/moe/marlin_moe_wna16/ops.cu:348, Invalid thread config: ... for MKN = [8192, 2688, 1856] and num_bits = 8, group_size = 32, ... max_shared_mem = 101376
```

Reproducer: `vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16 --quantization mxfp8` on an RTX PRO 6000 (intermediate size 1856).

Humming has no such limit and is the announced successor to Marlin, so the MXFP8 MoE backend selection now moves Humming directly ahead of Marlin on SM12x. The reorder is local to `oracle/mxfp8.py`, mirroring the SM11x/SM12x special case in `oracle/mxfp4.py`; `humming/priority.py` is untouched. Other compute capabilities and all other kernel families are unchanged. Marlin remains selectable with `--moe-backend marlin`.

## Test Plan

- `tests/kernels/quantization/test_scaled_mm_kernel_selection.py`: new parametrized case checks that on SM12x Humming is directly ahead of Marlin in the MXFP8 backend order, on non-SM12x Marlin stays ahead, and no other backend moves. Passes in the v0.32.0 container on an RTX PRO 6000 (live order: FLASHINFER_TRTLLM, DEEPGEMM, HUMMING, MARLIN, ...).
- RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120, 99 KB smem), vLLM v0.32.0 image with only `oracle/mxfp8.py` replaced.
- Nemotron 3 Nano BF16 `--quantization mxfp8`: stock selects MARLIN and crashes as above; patched selects HUMMING and serves.
- Decode-heavy A/B on a public MXFP8 MoE model that Marlin already handles (Qwen3-30B-A3B, `--quantization mxfp8`, forced via `--moe-backend`), `vllm bench serve`, random 1024 in / 256 out, `--ignore-eos`.
- GSM8K, lm_eval 5-shot, 1319 samples, chat template, `max_gen_toks=1024`, thinking disabled.

## Test Result

Qwen3-30B-A3B MXFP8, same shapes for both kernels:

| Concurrency | Metric | Marlin | Humming |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Median TPOT (ms) | 5.83 | 5.73 |
| 1 | Output tok/s | 164.8 | 166.3 |
| 1 | Median TTFT (ms) | 64.4 | 78.7 |
| 32 | Median TPOT (ms) | 19.60 | 19.69 |
| 32 | P99 TPOT (ms) | 24.21 | 23.53 |
| 32 | Output tok/s | 1346 | 1374 |
| 32 | Median TTFT (ms) | 671 | 505 |
| 32 | Median E2EL (ms) | 5633 | 5412 |

GSM8K exact_match (strict / flexible):

| Model | Backend | strict | flexible |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-30B-A3B MXFP8 | Marlin | 0.9105 ± 0.008 | 0.9181 ± 0.008 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B MXFP8 | Humming | 0.9075 ± 0.008 | 0.9158 ± 0.008 |
| Nemotron 3 Nano MXFP8 | Humming (patched; stock crashes) | 0.9075 ± 0.008 | 0.9067 ± 0.008 |

Decode is at parity within noise; at concurrency 32 Humming is slightly ahead on throughput, tail TPOT, TTFT and E2E. Accuracy is identical within stderr. Only SM120 was tested; SM121 (GB10) is included on the basis of its documented 99 KB shared-memory limit.

---

Thanks @stecasta, all good points. Reworked and re-tested:

1. **Perf / accuracy**: added a decode-heavy Marlin vs Humming A/B on Qwen3-30B-A3B `--quantization mxfp8` (shapes Marlin handles today, forced via `--moe-backend`), 1024 in / 256 out at concurrency 1 and 32: TPOT at parity (5.83 vs 5.73 ms at c=1, 19.60 vs 19.69 ms at c=32), Humming slightly ahead on throughput, P99 TPOT, TTFT and E2E at c=32. 2. **Mechanism**: took the local-reorder option. `priority.py` is back to main, no private import; the swap lives in `oracle/mxfp8.py` next to the existing `prioritize_humming` call, same shape as the SM11x/SM12x block in `oracle/mxfp4.py`. No overlap with #63561 / #63265.
3. **SM12x**: switched to `is_device_capability_family(120)` so GB10 is covered. Only SM120 was tested; noted in the description.
4. **Test**: dropped the new file; one parametrized case added to `test_scaled_mm_kernel_selection.py` (SM12x puts Humming directly ahead of Marlin, non-SM12x does not, nothing else moves). The global-default assertion is gone.

Net diff vs main is now 2 files, +42/-1. @mgoin could you add `ready` when you get a chance?

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Hi @marckarp,

1. This flips the default for every MXFP8 MoE model on SM120, not only the shapes where Marlin has no fitting tile. The perf table is an 8-output-token workload on a non-public checkpoint, so it is mostly prefill. Could you add decode-heavy numbers (BS1 and one higher concurrency, a few hundred output tokens) on a public MXFP8 MoE whose shapes Marlin handles today (e.g. `--quantization mxfp8` on Qwen3-30B-A3B), plus a GSM8K lm_eval on the Nemotron 3 Nano reproducer?
2. #63561 also changes the `prefers_humming` / `prioritize_humming` signature (an `mp_config` gate for SM100 int4 g128), and #63265 adds an `ahead_of` argument. Should we settle on one way for a caller to express a per-format preference before these land, so `priority.py` does not grow three independent knobs? Alternatively, a local reorder in the MXFP8 oracle (like the SM11x/SM12x block in `oracle/mxfp4.py`) would leave `priority.py` untouched and avoid importing the private `_HUMMING_PREFERRED_CAPABILITIES`.

IIUC GB10 (SM121, DGX Spark) has the same 99 KB opt-in shared memory limit, so the Nemotron 3 Nano MXFP8 reproducer should still pick Marlin and fail with `Invalid thread config` there. Should this cover the SM12x family (`{120, 121}`, or `is_device_capability_family(120)` as `oracle/mxfp4.py` does) rather than exact SM120?

@@ -0,0 +1,70 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""MXFP8 MoE backend priority: Humming outranks Marlin on SM120.
+
+GPU-free. On 99 KB shared-memory GPUs (SM120) the 8-bit Marlin MoE kernel has
+no fitting tile for expert shapes whose intermediate size is not a multiple of
+128 and fails at warm-up, so MXFP8 MoE backend selection widens the
+Humming-preferred set to include SM120 without touching the global default
+used by other formats.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.oracle.fp8 import Fp8MoeBackend
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.oracle.mxfp8 import (
+    _MXFP8_HUMMING_PREFERRED_CAPABILITIES,
+    _SUPPORTED_BACKENDS,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.humming.priority import (
+    _HUMMING_PREFERRED_CAPABILITIES,
+    prefers_humming,
+    prioritize_humming,
+)
+
+
+def _order(compute_capability: int, capabilities: frozenset[int]) -> list[str]:
+    return [
+        b.name
+        for b in prioritize_humming(
+            list(_SUPPORTED_BACKENDS),
+            compute_capability=compute_capability,
+            capabilities=capabilities,
+        )
+    ]
+
+
+def test_mxfp8_set_is_a_superset_of_the_global_set():
+    assert _HUMMING_PREFERRED_CAPABILITIES <= _MXFP8_HUMMING_PREFERRED_CAPABILITIES
+    assert 120 in _MXFP8_HUMMING_PREFERRED_CAPABILITIES
+
+
+def test_global_default_unchanged_on_sm120():
+    """Other kernel families keep their Marlin-first order on SM120."""
+    assert not prefers_humming(120)
+    assert prioritize_humming(
+        list(_SUPPORTED_BACKENDS), compute_capability=120
+    ) == list(_SUPPORTED_BACKENDS)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "compute_capability", sorted(_MXFP8_HUMMING_PREFERRED_CAPABILITIES)
+)
+def test_mxfp8_prefers_humming_over_marlin(compute_capability):
+    names = _order(compute_capability, _MXFP8_HUMMING_PREFERRED_CAPABILITIES)
+    humming = names.index(Fp8MoeBackend.HUMMING.name)
+    assert names[humming + 1] == Fp8MoeBackend.MARLIN.name
+    # Everything else keeps its relative order.
+    del names[humming]
+    assert names == [
+        b.name for b in _SUPPORTED_BACKENDS if b is not Fp8MoeBackend.HUMMING
+    ]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("compute_capability", [80, 86, 89, 100, 103])
+def test_mxfp8_keeps_marlin_first_elsewhere(compute_capability):
+    names = _order(compute_capability, _MXFP8_HUMMING_PREFERRED_CAPABILITIES)
+    assert names == [b.name for b in _SUPPORTED_BACKENDS]
+    assert names.index(Fp8MoeBackend.MARLIN.name) < names.index(
+        Fp8MoeBackend.HUMMING.name
+    )

+def _get_priority_backends() -> list[Fp8MoeBackend]:

@@ -0,0 +1,70 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""MXFP8 MoE backend priority: Humming outranks Marlin on SM120.
+
+GPU-free. On 99 KB shared-memory GPUs (SM120) the 8-bit Marlin MoE kernel has
+no fitting tile for expert shapes whose intermediate size is not a multiple of
+128 and fails at warm-up, so MXFP8 MoE backend selection widens the
+Humming-preferred set to include SM120 without touching the global default
+used by other formats.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.oracle.fp8 import Fp8MoeBackend
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.oracle.mxfp8 import (
+    _MXFP8_HUMMING_PREFERRED_CAPABILITIES,
+    _SUPPORTED_BACKENDS,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.humming.priority import (
+    _HUMMING_PREFERRED_CAPABILITIES,
+    prefers_humming,
+    prioritize_humming,
+)
+
+
+def _order(compute_capability: int, capabilities: frozenset[int]) -> list[str]:
+    return [
+        b.name
+        for b in prioritize_humming(
+            list(_SUPPORTED_BACKENDS),
+            compute_capability=compute_capability,
+            capabilities=capabilities,
+        )
+    ]
+
+
+def test_mxfp8_set_is_a_superset_of_the_global_set():
+    assert _HUMMING_PREFERRED_CAPABILITIES <= _MXFP8_HUMMING_PREFERRED_CAPABILITIES
+    assert 120 in _MXFP8_HUMMING_PREFERRED_CAPABILITIES
+
+
+def test_global_default_unchanged_on_sm120():
+    """Other kernel families keep their Marlin-first order on SM120."""
+    assert not prefers_humming(120)
+    assert prioritize_humming(
+        list(_SUPPORTED_BACKENDS), compute_capability=120
+    ) == list(_SUPPORTED_BACKENDS)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "compute_capability", sorted(_MXFP8_HUMMING_PREFERRED_CAPABILITIES)
+)
+def test_mxfp8_prefers_humming_over_marlin(compute_capability):
+    names = _order(compute_capability, _MXFP8_HUMMING_PREFERRED_CAPABILITIES)
+    humming = names.index(Fp8MoeBackend.HUMMING.name)
+    assert names[humming + 1] == Fp8MoeBackend.MARLIN.name
+    # Everything else keeps its relative order.
+    del names[humming]
+    assert names == [
+        b.name for b in _SUPPORTED_BACKENDS if b is not Fp8MoeBackend.HUMMING
+    ]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("compute_capability", [80, 86, 89, 100, 103])
+def test_mxfp8_keeps_marlin_first_elsewhere(compute_capability):
+    names = _order(compute_capability, _MXFP8_HUMMING_PREFERRED_CAPABILITIES)
+    assert names == [b.name for b in _SUPPORTED_BACKENDS]
+    assert names.index(Fp8MoeBackend.MARLIN.name) < names.index(
+        Fp8MoeBackend.HUMMING.name
+    )

Thanks @marckarp, since we've officially announced humming as the eventual replacement for marlin in vllm, I'd prefer to add the capability into humming/let humming be selected instead of marlin for this case

Makes sense, thanks. Reworked: Marlin is untouched. The MXFP8 MoE backend selection now prefers Humming over Marlin on SM120 (via an optional `capabilities` set on `prioritize_humming`, global default unchanged). Validated on an RTX PRO 6000 with the Nemotron 3 Nano online-MXFP8 reproducer (stock v0.32.0 still crashes, patched selects Humming and serves correctly) and, for perf, a second NVFP4 checkpoint with the same MXFP8 expert shape: Humming at parity with a locally patched Marlin from 2K to 112K tokens (numbers in the description). Scoped to SM120 only since that is what I could test; SM86/SM89 share the 99 KB limit if you want it widened.

Thanks @stecasta, all good points. Reworked and re-tested:

1. **Perf / accuracy**: added a decode-heavy Marlin vs Humming A/B on Qwen3-30B-A3B `--quantization mxfp8` (shapes Marlin handles today, forced via `--moe-backend`), 1024 in / 256 out at concurrency 1 and 32: TPOT at parity (5.83 vs 5.73 ms at c=1, 19.60 vs 19.69 ms at c=32), Humming slightly ahead on throughput, P99 TPOT, TTFT and E2E at c=32. GSM8K 5-shot full set: Qwen Marlin 0.9105 vs Humming 0.9075 strict (within stderr); Nemotron 3 Nano with Humming 0.9075 strict (stock crashes). Full tables in the description.
2. **Mechanism**: took the local-reorder option. `priority.py` is back to main, no private import; the swap lives in `oracle/mxfp8.py` next to the existing `prioritize_humming` call, same shape as the SM11x/SM12x block in `oracle/mxfp4.py`. No overlap with #63561 / #63265.
3. **SM12x**: switched to `is_device_capability_family(120)` so GB10 is covered. Only SM120 was tested; noted in the description.
4. **Test**: dropped the new file; one parametrized case added to `test_scaled_mm_kernel_selection.py` (SM12x puts Humming directly ahead of Marlin, non-SM12x does not, nothing else moves). The global-default assertion is gone.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Hi @marckarp,

1. This flips the default for every MXFP8 MoE model on SM120, not only the shapes where Marlin has no fitting tile. The perf table is an 8-output-token workload on a non-public checkpoint, so it is mostly prefill. Could you add decode-heavy numbers (BS1 and one higher concurrency, a few hundred output tokens) on a public MXFP8 MoE whose shapes Marlin handles today (e.g. `--quantization mxfp8` on Qwen3-30B-A3B), plus a GSM8K lm_eval on the Nemotron 3 Nano reproducer?
2. #63561 also changes the `prefers_humming` / `prioritize_humming` signature (an `mp_config` gate for SM100 int4 g128), and #63265 adds an `ahead_of` argument. Should we settle on one way for a caller to express a per-format preference before these land, so `priority.py` does not grow three independent knobs? Alternatively, a local reorder in the MXFP8 oracle (like the SM11x/SM12x block in `oracle/mxfp4.py`) would leave `priority.py` untouched and avoid importing the private `_HUMMING_PREFERRED_CAPABILITIES`.
Hi @marckarp, thanks for the rework. LGTM, one note on the test inline.
